audit.whatIsWrong: Three rows disagreed across layers: full phases[3] and phases[5] read 'Skill' and phases[6] read 'Veigar', while content win[3], win[5] and win[6] all read 'Zed' — and the packet agrees with content on all seven.
audit.why: Zed is 54.45% over 2733 games. Veigar is among the least mobile mids: no dash, no shield, and one defensive tool on a 20-second cooldown at rank 1. Every stage of the lane is Zed's provided the cage is respected.
audit.corrected: All three full sides moved to Zed. Each of those rows' whys already described Zed winning, and the content layer already read Zed, so no paired win[N] edits were proposed — they would have been no-ops.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3] sat at 5/10 in a lane the page and the data both call Zed's throughout.
audit.why: Levels 4-5 are exactly when Zed's E is on a 3.5s cooldown and Veigar's cage is still 20s — the widest tempo gap of the lane.
audit.corrected: phases[3].rating raised to 6/10 to match the surrounding rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Primordial Burst scales on the TARGET'S MISSING HEALTH — the lower you are, the harder it hits. The page never said so, and its whole framing is 'chip to 60% then commit', which is the state that makes his ult lethal to you. Event Horizon's real cooldown, the number that decides every commit, was also absent.
audit.why: Riot's R text: dealing a large amount of magic damage, increasing based on the target's missing health. Riot's E text: only enemies that PASS THROUGH the cage are stunned, which is why a shadow-angle entry works and a dash into the wall does not.
audit.corrected: Written into tradeBad, breakdown.trading, breakdown.cooldowns, enemyWin and breakdown.carry.

audit.why: It is the field that carries the numbers, and Event Horizon's 20s is the single most actionable number in this matchup.
audit.corrected: Event Horizon 20s at rank 1 and 14s maxed, Baleful Strike 6s to 4s at 1000 range, Primordial Burst 120/90/60, Living Shadow 20s.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.feeding was generic and missed the one thing that makes feeding Veigar different: Phenomenal Evil Power is PERMANENT ability power from spell hits and takedowns.
audit.why: Riot's passive text: striking an enemy champion with a spell or scoring a takedown grants permanently increased ability power. Baleful Strike kills also bank it.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to say that a kill banks permanent AP and that denying last hits is the real currency.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim, both under unrelated titles.
audit.why: The heading and body described different things.
audit.corrected: Both replaced with bodies that answer their own titles.

edits.before: - Veigar Event Horizon (Cage): matchup-defining — Only the cage EDGE stuns — hold position near the center or leave before it forms; never dash into the wall. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Living Shadow (swap) like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Event Horizon is 20s at rank 1 and still 14s maxed — the longest punish window in the lane, and only its edge stuns. - Baleful Strike is 6s to 4s at 1000 range. - Primordial Burst is 120/90/60 and grows with your MISSING health, so do not sit low. - Living Shadow is 20s.

notes: The full layer's phases[6] read 'Veigar' against both the content layer and the packet, which read 'Zed'. I moved it to Zed to make the page self-consistent, and the row's existing why already describes Zed picking late — but flagging it honestly: Veigar's uncapped Phenomenal Evil scaling is a real argument for the two-item row belonging to him, and if the user wants that verdict the correct fix is the opposite move, flipping content win[6] and whys[6] to Veigar as a pair.
